title: 5-Year Treasury Note auction (December new issue) — pulled onto the 2-Year's own Monday session, the schedule's only doubled coupon day
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes), text layer decompressed stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 213 rows by the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-12-24 initial research. The row reads `5-Year  NOTE`, announced `Thursday, December 24, 2026`, auctioned `Monday, December 28, 2026`, settling `Thursday, December 31, 2026`. No trailing `R` against the document's own legend (`R --denotes reopening`), so it is a new issue; it is also distinct from the `5-Year  TIPS R T` row announced 2026-12-17, which is a different security. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-12-24 announcement itself. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-09 by the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-12-24 never-assessed initial research, which owns the announcement that sizes this auction. WHY IT IS A GAP AND NOT A DUPLICATE: this calendar already tracks the 5-Year's August, September, October and November auctions (treasury-5y-note-2026-08-26, -2026-09-23, -2026-10-27, -2026-11-24) and the January one (treasury-5y-note-2027-01-26); December is the missing member of an established monthly series. WHAT MAKES IT WORTH ITS OWN ROW: this is the leg that MOVED. In every other month-end block in the schedule's window the 5-Year gets its own session the day after the 2-Year; here it is pulled forward onto the 2-Year's Monday, making 2026-12-28 the only doubled coupon day in the window and the block a 2-session block rather than a 3-session one. The proposing research measured that compression at the block level across 125 blocks since 2015 and found this calendar's first non-null: the 2Y/5Y pair in a compressed block averages z -0.237 against +0.062 elsewhere (t=-1.42 full sample; t=-2.67 from 2020-05, n=7 and t=-1.75 in the current size regime), with a clean placebo — the 7-Year, which keeps its own session, shows nothing in any window (t=-0.17). Score that hypothesis rather than re-deriving it; the pre-2020 sign flip rests on n=4 and is uninformative. SIZE EXPECTATION, carried not derived: $70B. sb0590's 5-Year column reads 70 in all six published rows (May-26 through Oct-26) and the tape has not moved it since 2024-04-24 — 28 auctions. Pool bid-to-cover mean is 2.425 (n=134 since 2015), the tightest-dispersed of the three legs (sd 0.106); the 2024-05-onward observed floor is 2.28. A DATA TRAP THE JANUARY SIBLING RECORDED AND THIS AUCTION INHERITS: 43 rows of 5-Year TIPS file as `security_type: Note`, `security_term: 5-Year` in fiscaldata, and `original_security_term` is itself mislabelled on 16 note rows — the robust filter is the intersection of both term fields plus `floating_rate: No` and `inflation_index_security: No`, or the last-size-change date comes back wrong. THE DIRECT PRECEDENT is 2020-12-28, a row-for-row calendar twin sharing its session with that year's 2-Year exactly as this one does, which printed 2.39 — z -0.33. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook is rates-keyed.
